hook_text: Water just knee-deep can knock you off your feet. Water up to your waist can float a car.
clip_script: April 2022. A cut-off low parks itself over KwaZulu-Natal, and in parts of eThekwini more than three hundred millimetres of rain falls in about a day. That's more than a whole year of rain in some parts of the Karoo. The ground fills up. Roofs, roads and paving send water racing into rivers. Rivers burst their banks. Bridges vanish. Homes on river banks are swept away. The port of Durban shuts down. More than four hundred people die, many of them trying to cross flooded roads and rivers. Floods are South Africa's most common disaster, and people make them worse by clearing vegetation and covering the ground with concrete. One rule can save your life: if it's flooded, forget it.
visual_style: A whiteboard rain gauge overflowing; a cross-section of rain hitting grass versus concrete with arrows of run-off; a river rising over a bridge; a road sign reading If it's flooded, forget it.
pacing: Scary fact hook, a fast storm story, a calm safety rule.
